## RTS player arousal — UI analysis (live-play session 2026-05-23)

### Where it lives in the UI

Left sidebar, third caption-card from top:
1. Your Outfit (clothing preview)
2. Corruption (`Pure 😇` + points counter)
3. **🔆 Energy & Arousal** ← arousal lives here, paired with energy
4. Money (Cash $)
5. Stats (Exhibitionism / Intelligence / Beauty)

Inside the Energy & Arousal card, two horizontal progress widgets stacked vertically:
- top: energy bar (🔋 100%)
- bottom: arousal bar (❄️ Calm at zero state)

Both rendered with the same wrapper / container / bar / fill / overlay-text pattern. The energy bar shows a raw percentage as overlay text; the arousal bar shows an **emoji + band-name** as overlay text — there's no number, just the band word.

### DOM structure

```html
<div class="arousal-wrapper">
  <div class="arousal-progress-container">
    <div class="arousal-progress-bar">
      <div class="arousal-progress-fill {low|medium|high}" style="width: N%;"></div>
      <span class="arousal-progress-text">{icon} {bandText}</span>
    </div>
  </div>
  <div class="arousal-tooltip">Arousal</div>
</div>
```

The `.arousal-tooltip` is an absolute-positioned hover bubble that reveals the literal word "Arousal" on `:hover` — i.e. there's no static label outside the bar itself; the band word IS the label.

### Renderer (SugarCube `<<ArousalDisplay>>` macro)

```js
Macro.add('ArousalDisplay', { handler: function () {
  var currentArousal = game().player.arousal;
  var maxArousal = game().game.maxArousal;             // = 10
  var percentage = Math.floor((currentArousal / maxArousal) * 100);
  var arousalClass = percentage > 70 ? 'high'
                   : percentage > 40 ? 'medium'
                   : 'low';
  var arousalLevel = currentArousal === 0
                   ? 0
                   : Math.min(Math.ceil((currentArousal / maxArousal) * 4), 4);
  var { icon, text } = LeftBarService.getArousalText(arousalLevel);
  // … builds DOM (wrapper → container → bar → fill + text + tooltip) …
}});
```

### Band table (`LeftBarService.getArousalText`)

| Level | Icon | Text |
|---|---|---|
| 0 | ❄️ | Calm |
| 1 | 🔥 | Warm |
| 2 | 🔥 | Aroused |
| 3 | 🔥 | Hot |
| 4 | 🔥 | Burning |

`default` falls back to ❄️ Calm.

### Color tiers (CSS)

| Class | Threshold | Gradient | Glow |
|---|---|---|---|
| `low` | `percentage ≤ 40` | `linear-gradient(90deg, #2196f3 → #1976d2)` (blue) | `0 0 8px rgba(33,150,243,.3)` |
| `medium` | `percentage > 40 && ≤ 70` | `linear-gradient(90deg, #ff9800 → #ff5722)` (orange) | `0 0 8px rgba(255,152,0,.3)` |
| `high` | `percentage > 70` | `linear-gradient(90deg, #ff6b6b → #ff1744)` (red) | `0 0 8px rgba(255,107,107,.3)` |

Both `width` and the gradient change get a `transition: width 0.6s cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)` so increments animate smoothly.

### Full value table (arousal ∈ {0..10}, maxArousal=10)

Verified empirically by mutating `player.arousal` and re-invoking `Macro.get('ArousalDisplay').handler.call({output: sandbox}, …)`:

| arousal | % width | color class | level | text | tier color |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | 0% | `low` | 0 | ❄️ Calm | blue |
| 1 | 10% | `low` | 1 | 🔥 Warm | blue |
| 2 | 20% | `low` | 1 | 🔥 Warm | blue |
| 3 | 30% | `low` | 2 | 🔥 Aroused | blue |
| 4 | 40% | `low` | 2 | 🔥 Aroused | blue |
| 5 | 50% | `medium` | 2 | 🔥 Aroused | orange |
| 6 | 60% | `medium` | 3 | 🔥 Hot | orange |
| 7 | 70% | `medium` | 3 | 🔥 Hot | orange |
| 8 | 80% | `high` | 4 | 🔥 Burning | red |
| 9 | 90% | `high` | 4 | 🔥 Burning | red |
| 10 | 100% | `high` | 4 | 🔥 Burning | red |

### Key design observations

1. **No raw number ever shown.** Energy displays "🔋 100%" but arousal displays only the band word (Calm/Warm/Aroused/Hot/Burning). The player learns arousal qualitatively, not numerically.

2. **Color tier and text tier are decoupled by design.** Arousal 3 = "Aroused" text but blue (low) fill. Arousal 5 = same "Aroused" text but orange (medium) fill. This means the bar's *color* communicates one signal (cool/warm/hot range) and the *word* communicates a separate finer-grained signal (5 bands).

3. **Asymmetric band boundaries on the text axis.** Calm is a single integer (0); Warm spans 2 (1–2); Aroused spans 2 (3–4); but the medium-color tier captures arousal 5 ALSO as "Aroused" — text-tier "Aroused" straddles two color tiers. Hot spans 2 (6–7); Burning spans 3 (8–10). So the visible widget changes either text OR color on most increments, never both at the same boundary except at arousal 8 (text → Burning AND color → high red).

4. **Single emoji vocabulary.** Only two icons: ❄️ for "Calm" (the zero state), 🔥 for everything else. No graduated emoji ramp (e.g. 💧→🌡️→🔥) — once you're above zero, you're on fire.

5. **No decay surfacing.** The widget renders only the current value; there's no countdown, no "decaying soon" warning, no recent-change indicator. (Per prior memory, RTS player arousal is no-decay anyway — sleep raises it, climax zeroes it, otherwise monotone.)

6. **Hover-only label.** "Arousal" word itself appears only on hover via `.arousal-tooltip`. The card title "🔆 Energy & Arousal" identifies the group, but the bar's own label is implicit from emoji+band.

7. **Same render shape as energy.** Energy and arousal share `*-wrapper / *-progress-container / *-progress-bar / *-progress-fill / *-progress-text / *-tooltip` class skeleton. Only the fill-tier color gradients and the overlay-text vocabulary differ. Implication: a designer wanting to add a third bar (e.g. "Hunger", "Stress") inherits the layout for free.
